title: SFO, OAK or SJC? Choosing an Airport for a Silicon Valley Business Trip
description: Compare SFO, OAK and SJC using your meeting addresses, flight options and return plans, with a practical airport-choice checklist for Silicon Valley trips.
cta: Choose the airport, then plan the complete transfer.
image_alt: Three silver aircraft on separate discs linked by orange paths to one office building on a charcoal background.
body:
For a Silicon Valley business trip, start with SJC when your schedule centers on San Jose or Santa Clara, compare SFO for Peninsula meetings or a trip that also includes San Francisco, and consider OAK when the East Bay or a better flight schedule makes it relevant. Then check the actual addresses and both travel days. These are starting points for a comparison, not a universal ranking.

The right airport is the one whose flight and ground journey work together. A convenient landing time can lose its advantage if the hotel or first meeting is on the other side of the region.

Put three addresses beside your flight search

Write down your first destination after landing, your hotel and your final stop before the return flight. Use street addresses and the correct campus or building entrance. A company name or “Silicon Valley” is too broad to estimate a transfer.

Compare the inbound journey to the first stop and the outbound journey from the last stop separately. If your schedule ends somewhere different from where it begins, flying into one airport and out of another may be worth pricing. Confirm the ticket arrangement and both ground transfers before committing.

SJC: start here for a South Bay schedule

San José Mineta International Airport is in San Jose, close to downtown; the airport's visitor overview places it as a gateway to Silicon Valley. For meetings in San Jose or Santa Clara, SJC is a useful first option to evaluate. For Sunnyvale, Mountain View or a campus farther away, compare the exact route against SFO rather than assuming one airport always wins.

Check SJC's official nonstop destinations, then verify service on your dates directly with the airline. A route listing does not mean every flight operates daily or year-round. If the available itinerary requires a connection, compare its total journey with a nonstop into another airport.

SFO: compare for Peninsula meetings and mixed city trips

SFO is on the San Francisco Peninsula in San Mateo County, south of San Francisco, as described in the airport's official overview. It deserves a close look when your trip includes San Mateo, Redwood City, other Peninsula stops or time in San Francisco before heading south.

For Palo Alto or Menlo Park, compare both SFO and SJC using the actual arrival time and meeting address. Do not choose from straight-line distance alone. Use SFO's flight information and nonstop-service resources to explore flights, and confirm the schedule with the airline. A suitable nonstop can be a meaningful advantage even when its airport is farther from the meeting.

OAK: include it when the East Bay or flight schedule matters

OAK is in Oakland on the East Bay side of the region. It is worth considering when your itinerary includes Oakland or another East Bay stop, or when its flight options fit your plans particularly well. Consult OAK's official airline and destination resource before comparing the complete journey.

For a trip centered on Peninsula or South Bay meetings, look carefully at the ground leg before choosing OAK on airfare alone. The road route depends on the destination; do not assume every journey uses a bridge. OAK's official driving directions identify airport access from I-880. Check a current route estimate for the day and time you expect to travel.

Compare the time you can actually use

Scheduled landing is not the time you will arrive at the meeting. Allow for leaving the aircraft, collecting checked bags, any required entry formalities, reaching the agreed pickup and the drive. Add a margin for delays instead of filling the whole gap with scheduled activities.

For the return, work backward from your airline's recommended airport-arrival time and check-in deadlines. Include any hotel or luggage stop before the airport. Ask the transportation provider to review the route and pickup plan; a road-time estimate is not a guaranteed arrival time.

Three example comparisons
San Jose meetings and a Santa Clara hotel: compare suitable SJC flights first, then see whether a nonstop or better schedule at SFO changes the overall trip.
Palo Alto meetings followed by a night in San Francisco: compare SFO and SJC for arrival, then assess the departure from the San Francisco hotel independently.
An Oakland meeting followed by a South Bay stay: include OAK in the inbound search, but estimate the later transfer south too. The first convenient stop does not settle the whole itinerary.

A checklist to compare two flight options

Fill out the same details for each candidate before buying the ticket:

  • Airport and date: record SFO, OAK or SJC explicitly for each direction.
  • Flight: nonstop or connecting, scheduled arrival, return departure and service confirmed for your dates.
  • Addresses: first stop, hotel and final stop before departure.
  • Ground plan: route estimate at the expected travel time, extra stops and a delay margin.
  • Cost: airfare with the bags and flexibility you need, plus a quote for each ground transfer.
  • Travel party: passengers, luggage and any equipment or assistance requirements to confirm with the operator.
  • Schedule tolerance: what happens if the flight is late or the final meeting runs over?

Once you choose the flights, send the confirmed airport codes, flight details, addresses and luggage count when arranging Koast airport transfers. Our SFO, OAK and SJC service pages provide the next step for the airport you select.
